questions.q: Let the solution curve $y = y ( x )$ of the differential equation~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{3x^{5}\tan^{- 1}\left(x^{3}\right)}{\left(1 + x^{6}\right)\dfrac{3}{2}}y = 2x$~$exp\dfrac{x^{3} - \tan^{- 1}x^{3}}{( 1 + x{)}^{6}}$~pass through the origin. Then~$y ( 1 )$& is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{- 3x^{5}\tan^{- 1}\left(x^{3}\right)}{\left(1 + x^{6}\right)3 / 2}\right)y = 2xe\left\{\dfrac{x^{3} - \tan^{- 1}x^{3}}{\left(1 + x\right)6}\right\}$

This is a linear differential equation of the form~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$.

Hence,

$I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{- 3x^{5}\tan^{- 1}x^{3}}{\left(1 + x^{6}\right)3 / 2}dx}$

Put~$\tan^{- 1}x^{3} = u ⇒ \left(\dfrac{3x^{2}}{1 + x^{6}}\right)dx = du$

$I . F . = e^{- ∫ \dfrac{utanu}{1 + \tan^{2}u}du}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{- ∫ \dfrac{utanu}{secu}du}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{- ∫ usinudu}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{- \left[- ucosu + ∫ cosudu\right]}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{ucosu - sinu}$

$⇒ I . F . = e\left\{\tan^{- 1}\left(x^{3}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + x^{6}}\right) - \left(\dfrac{x3}{1 + x^{6}}\right)\right\}$

$⇒ I . F . = e\left\{\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}x^{3} - x^{3}}{1 + x^{6}}\right\}$

Solution of differential equation is

$y \cdot e\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}x^{3} - x^{3}}{1 + x^{6}} = ∫ 2xe\left(\dfrac{x^{3} - \tan^{- 1}x^{3}}{1 + x^{6}}\right) \cdot e\left(\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}\left(x^{3}\right) - x^{3}}{1 + x^{6}}\right)dx$

$⇒ y \cdot e\left\{\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}x^{3} - x^{3}}{1 + x^{6}}\right\} = ∫ 2xdx$

$⇒ y \cdot e\left\{\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}x^{3} - x^{3}}{1 + x^{6}}\right\} = x^{2} + C$

Also, it passes through the origin then~$C = 0$, hence

$ye\left\{\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}x^{3} - x^{3}}{1 + x^{6}}\right\} = x^{2}$

Now, put~$x = 1$, then we get

$y\left(1\right)e\dfrac{\tan^{- 1}\left(1\right) - 1}{2} = 1$

$⇒ y\left(1\right)e\dfrac{\pi - 4}{4\sqrt{2}} = 1$

$⇒ y\left(1\right) = \dfrac{1}{e\left(\dfrac{\pi - 4}{4\sqrt{2}}\right)}$

$⇒ y\left(1\right) = e\dfrac{4 - \pi}{4\sqrt{2}}$

questions.q: If $y = y  \left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation $, e^{y}  \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx} -1\right) = e^{x}$ such that $y\left(0\right) = 0,$ then $y\left(1\right)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$e^{y} = t$
$e^{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$
$\dfrac{dt}{dx} - t = e^{x}$
$IF = e^{- ∫ dx}$

$⇒ t \cdot e^{- x} = x + 1$
$e^{y - x} = x + 1$
$y = x + ln ⁡ \left(x + 1\right)$
at $x = 1, y = 1 + ln ⁡ \left(2\right)$

questions.q:
Let $\alpha$ be a non-zero real number. Suppose $f: R \to R$ is a differentiable function such that $f\left(0\right) = 1$ and $\lim_{x \to - \infty}f\left(x\right) = 1$. If $f^{'} \left(x\right) = \alphaf \left($x\right) + 3$, for all $x \in \mathbb{R},$ then f\left(- \log_{\mathrm{e}}$2\right)$ is equal to ________.

$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given: $f\left(0\right) = 1, \lim_{x \to - \infty}f\left(x\right) = 1$

And $f^{'}\left(x\right) - \alpha \cdot f\left(x\right) = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \alpha \cdot y = 3$

Which is a linear differential equation, so

$⇒ I . F . = e^{- \alphax}$

Solution of the differential equation is given by,

$y\left(e^{- \alphax}\right) = ∫ 3 \cdot e^{- \alphax}dx$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) ⋅ \left(e^{- \alphax}\right) = \dfrac{3e^{- \alphax}}{- \alpha} + c$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{- 3}{α} + c \cdot e^{\alphax}$

Now, taking case I: when $\alpha > 0$ and $\lim_{x \to - \infty}f \left(x\right) = 1$ we get,

$⇒ 1 = $\dfrac{- 3}{α} ++$c\left($0\right)$

\alpha = -$3$ (rejected)

Case-II: \alpha$< 0$

as $\lim_{x \to - $\i$infty}f \left($x\right) = 1$

$⇒ c = 0 & \dfrac{- 3}{α} ==$1\left\${\text{as}$e^{- \left(- \infty\right)} \to $\infty , \text{so}$c = 0\right\}$

$⇒ $\alpha = -$3$

$⇒ $f\left($x\right) = 1$ and also f\left($0\right) = 1$

Hence, f\left($x\right) = 1$ is constant function, so f\left(- \log_{\mathrm{e}}$2\right) = 1$

questions.q: If& $y = y  \left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation 2x^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} -$2xy + 3y^{2} = 0$~such that $y  \left(e\right) = \dfrac{e}{3},$then $y\left(1\right)$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $2x^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2xy + 3y^{2} = 0$

Dividing by $2x^{2}y^{2}$, we get,

$- \dfrac{1}{y2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{1}{xy} = \dfrac{3}{2x^{2}}$

Let~$\dfrac{1}{y} = p, \dfrac{- 1}{y2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dp}{dx}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dp}{dx} + \dfrac{1}{x}\left(p\right) = \dfrac{3}{2x^{2}}$

General~solution will be $p \cdot e^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = ∫ \dfrac{3}{2x^{2}}{·}^{e∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx}dx + c$
$⇒ \dfrac{x}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{3}{2x}dx + c ⇒ \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{3}{2}lnx + c$

$∵ y\left(e\right) = \dfrac{e}{3} ⇒ c = \dfrac{3}{2} ⇒ \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{3}{2}lnx + \dfrac{3}{2}$~is the particular solution.

when~$x = 1; y\left(1\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}$

questions.q: If $cosx\dfrac{dy}{dx} - ysinx = 6x$,  \left(0 < x < \dfrac{π}{2}\right)$ and $y $\$left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) =0,$ then y\left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$The given $D . E .$ can be written as

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} - ytanx = 6xsecx . . . \left(i\right),$~which is a liner differential equation of the form~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q,$~where~$P \text{ and } Q$~are the function of~$x$~or constants.

Here,~$P = - tanx \text{ and } Q = 6xsecx$

Integrating factor $= e^{∫ Pdx} = e^{- ∫ tanxdx}$

$= e^{- \left(- ln\left(cosx\right)\right)} = e^{ln\left(cosx\right)} = cosx$

And, the solution of the linear differential equation is,

$y\left(I . F .\right) = ∫ Q\left(I . F .\right)dx + c$

~$⇒ y ⋅ cosx = ∫ \left(6xsecx\right) ⋅ cosxdx$

$⇒ y ⋅ cosx = ∫ 6xdx$

$⇒ y \cdot cosx = 3x^{2} + c . . . \left(ii\right)$

Given y \left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right) =$0,$ hence

$0 = $3\$left(\dfrac{π}{3}\right)2 + c$

$⇒ c = - \dfrac{\pi2}{3}$

Thus, the curve is,~$y \cdotcosx = 3x^{2} - \dfrac{\pi2}{3}$

Now, put $x = \dfrac{π}{6},$~to~get

y \left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) \cdotcos $\$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) ==$3\$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)2 - \dfrac{\pi2}{3}$

$⇒ $y \$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)$⋅ $\dfrac{3}{2} =$3 ⋅ $\dfrac{\pi2}{36} - \dfrac{\pi2}{3}

$⇒ $y $\$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)⋅ \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{\pi2}{12} - \dfrac{\pi2}{3}$

$⇒ $y \$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right)$⋅ $\dfrac{3}{2} = - \dfrac{\pi2}{4}

$⇒ y\$left(\dfrac{π}{6}\right) = - \dfrac{\pi2}{2\sqrt{3}} .

$

questions.q: $If a curve $y = f  \left(x\right)$, passing through the point  \left(1, 2\right)$, is the solution of the differential equation~$2x^{2}dy =  \left($2xy + y^{2}\right)dx$, then $f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{y2}{2x^{2}}$

$⇒ y^{- 2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{y} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2x^{2}}$

Put~$- \dfrac{1}{y} = t ⇒ \dfrac{1}{y2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dx} + \left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)t = \dfrac{1}{2x^{2}}$~

This is a linear~differential equation,

with~Integrating Factor :~$e^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = e^{ln\left(x\right)} = x$~

So, solution of the linear differential equation is $tx = ∫ \dfrac{1}{2x^{2}} \cdot xdx + C$

$⇒ - \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{1}{2}ln \left(x\right) + C$

~The curve passes through~\left(1, 2\right)$

~$⇒ - $\dfrac{1}{2} = \ddfrac{1}{2}$ln\left($1\right) + C ⇒ C = - \dfrac{1}{2}$~

Hence, the particular solution to the differential equation is~$- \dfrac{x}{y} = \ddfrac{1}{2}$ln\left(x\right) - $\dfrac{1}{2}~

$⇒ $\dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{1 - ln\left(x\right)}{2}$⇒ y = $\dfrac{2x}{1 - ln\left(x\right)}

$⇒ f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}}{1 - ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{1 + ln\left(2\right)} = \dfrac{1}{1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(2\right)}$

$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be a solution curve of the differential equation  \left(y + 1\right)\tan^{2}xdx + tanxdy + ydx = 0$, $x \in \left(0, \dfrac{π}{2}\right)$. If $\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}xy \left($x\right) = 1, then the value of y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right)is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

\left(y + 1\right)\tan^{2}xdx + tanxdy + ydx = 0$

$⇒ \left[\left(y + 1\right)\tan^{2}x + y\right]dx + tanxdy = 0$

$⇒ tanx\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) + \left(y + 1\right)\tan^{2}x + y = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(1 + y\right)tanx = - ycotx$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\left(tanx + cotx\right) = - tanx$

This is a linear differential equation of the form~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + P \left($x\right)y = Q \left($x\right)$.

\text{I.F} =$e^{∫ ( tanx + cotx ) dx}$

$= e^{∫ \left(\dfrac{\tan^{2}x + 1}{tanx}\right)$dx}$

$= e^{∫ $\$left(\dfrac{\sec^{2}x}{tanx}\right)dx}$

$= e^{\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left|tanx\right|}$

$= tanx\left(∵ x \in \left(0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)\right)

Solution is

$ytanx = ∫ - \tan^{2}xdx + c$

$⇒ ytanx = ∫ \left(1 - \sec^{2}x\right)dx + c$

$⇒ ytanx = x - tanx + c$

Now,

$\lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}xy = 1$

$⇒ \lim_{x \to {0}^{+}}\left(\dfrac{x}{tanx}\$right)\left(x - tanx + c\right) = 1$

$⇒ 1 ( 0 - 0 + c ) = 1 ⇒ c = 1$

Then the function is

$ytanx = x - tanx + 1$

Put~$x = \dfrac{π}{4},$

$y\$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\rright)$tan\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) --tan\$left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) +$1$

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{π}{4}

questions.q: Let $\alphax = exp  \left(x^{β}y^{γ}\right)$ be the solution of the differential equation $2x^{2}ydy - \left(1 - xy^{2}\right)dx = 0$, $x > 0, y\left(2\right) = $\sqrt{\log_{\mathrm{e}}2}.Then $\alpha + \beta - \gammaequals:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given the solution of differential equation,

$\alphax = e^{x^{β} \cdot y^{γ}} . . . . . . ( 1 )$

Now calculating~the solution of differential equation,~

$2x^{2}y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 - xy^{2}$

Let~$y^{2} = t ⇒ 2\dfrac{d y}{d x} = \dfrac{d t}{d x}$

$∴ x^{2}\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 1 - xt$

$\dfrac{dt}{dx} + \dfrac{t}{x} = \dfrac{1}{x2} . . . . . ( 2 )$

Above differential equation is linear in~$t$

We know solutions of differential~equation of the form~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + Py = Q$~is given by,

$y . e^{∫ Pdx} = ∫ Q . e^{∫ Pdx} + C ( e^{∫ Pdx} = I . F . )$

Now calculating,~$I . F . = e^{∫ \dfrac{1}{x}dx} = e^{lnx} = x$

Therefore,~the solution of equation~ \left(2\right)$~is given by,

$t . x = ∫ \dfrac{1}{x2} \cdot xdx + C$

$⇒ y^{2} \cdot x = lnx + C$

$∵ y ( 2 ) = \sqrt{ln2}$

$∴ 2 . ln2 = ln2 + C ⇒ C = ln2$

Hence, solution is~$xy^{2} = lnx + ln2$

~$⇒ xy^{2} = ln2x$

$⇒ 2x = e^{x \cdot y^{2}} . . . . . . ( 3 )$

On comparing equations \left(1\right)$~and \left(3\right)$~we get,

~$\alpha = 2, \beta = 1, \gamma = 2$

$∴ \alpha + \beta - \gamma = 1$

$

questions.q: Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(\cos x\left(\log _{\mathrm{e}}(\cos$x)\right)^2 $\mathrm{dy}+  \left(\sinx-3 y \sin x \log _{\mathrm{e}}$(\cos x)\right)$\mathrm{d}$x=0, x \$in  \left($0, $\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$\). If \$(y \left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{-1}{\log _{\mathrm{e}} 2}\), then \(y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\) is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{3 \sin x}{\cos x \ln \cos x} y=-\frac{\sin x}{\cos x(\ln \cos x)^2} \\ & \text { I.F. }=e^{-\int \frac{3 \tan x}{\ln \cos x} d x} \\ & \text { Let } \ln \cos x=t \\ & -\tan x d x=d t \\ & e^{3 \int^{\frac{d t}{t}}}=e^{3 \ln t}=t^3=(\ln \cos x)^3 \\ & \therefore \quad \text { Solution will be } \\ & \quad y(\ln \cos x)^3=-\int(\tan x)(\ln \cos x) d x \\ & y(\ln \cos x)^3=\frac{(\ln \cos x)^2}{2}+c \\ & \because \quad y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=-\frac{1}{\ln 2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad c=0 \\ & \therefore \quad y=\frac{1}{2(\ln \cos x)} \\ & y\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{\ln \left(\cos \frac{\pi}{6}\right)} \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{1}{\ln \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)}\right] \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{\ln \sqrt{3}-\ln 2} \\ & =\frac{1}{\ln 3-\ln 4}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $Let the solution curve $y = y  \left(x\right)$~of the differential equation \left($1 + e^{2x}\$right)\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx} +y\right) = 1$~pass through the point  \left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right). Then, $\lim_{x \to $\infty}e^{x}y \left(x\right)& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

\left(1 + e^{2x}\right)\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\right) = 1$

Now on rearranging we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{2x}}$

We can see it is a linear differential equation,

So integrating factor is~$e^{∫ 1 \cdot dx} = e^{x}$

So solution will be

$y \cdot IF = ∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{2x}} \times IFdx$

$⇒ ye^{x} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{1 + e^{2x}} \times e^{x}dx$

~$⇒ y \cdot e^{x} = \tan^{- 1} \left($e^{x}\right) + c$

Now as curve is passing through~\left($0, $\dfrac{π}{2}\right)~so~

$⇒ c = $\dfrac{π}{4}

Now calculating the limit~$\lim_{x \to $\infty} \left(y \cdot e^{x}\right)$~we get,

$⇒ \lim_{x \to \infty}\left(y \cdot e^{x}\right) = \lim_{x \to \infty}\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(e^{x}\right) + \dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{π}{2} + \dfrac{π}{4} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

$

questions.q: If $y=y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation $\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}+2 y=\sin (2 x), y(0)=\frac{3}{4}$, then $y  \left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right)is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}+2 y=\sin 2 x, y(0)=\frac{3}{4} \\ & \text { I.F }=e^{\int 2 d x}=e^{2 x} \\ & y \cdot e^{2 x}=\int e^{2 x} \sin 2 x d x \\ & y \cdot e^{2 x}=\frac{e^{2 x}(2 \sin 2 x-2 \cos 2 x)}{4+4}+C \\ & x=0, y=\frac{3}{4} \Rightarrow \frac{3}{4} \cdot 1=\frac{1(0-2)}{8}+C \\ & \frac{3}{4}=-\frac{1}{4}+C \\ & 1=C \\ & y=\frac{2 \sin 2 x-2 \cos 2 x}{8}+1 \cdot e^{-2 x} \\ & x=\frac{\pi}{8}, y=\frac{1}{8}\left(2 \sin \frac{\pi}{4}-2 \cos \frac{\pi}{4}\right)+e^{-2\left(\frac{\pi}{8}\right)} \\ & y=0+e^{-\frac{\pi}{4}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If the curve $y = y ( x )$ is the solution of the differential equation $2\left(x^{2} + x^{5 / 4}\right)dy - y\left(x + x^{1 / 4}\right)dx = 2x^{9 / 4}dx, x > 0$~which passes through the point \left(1, 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2\right),$~then the value of $y ( 16 )$ \text{ and } is equal to \text{ and } <gwmw style="display:none;"></gwmw>$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given differential equation is& $2\left(x^{2} + x^{5 / 4}\right)dy - y\left(x + x^{1 / 4}\right)dx = 2x^{9 / 4}dx$

$⇒ 2\left(x^{2} + x^{5 / 4}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y\left(x + x^{1 / 4}\right) = 2x^{9 / 4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y\left(x + x^{1 / 4}\right)}{2\left(x^{2} + x^{5 / 4}\right)} = \dfrac{2x^{9 / 4}}{2\left(x^{2} + x^{5 / 4}\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y\left(x + x^{1 / 4}\right)}{2x\left(x + x^{1 / 4}\right)} = \dfrac{2x^{9 / 4}}{2x^{5 / 4} \left(x^{3 / 4} + 1\right)}$

$⇒ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{2x} ==$x\left($x^{3 / 4} + 1\right)$

This is a linear differential equation of the type~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} +Py = Q,$~where~$P = - \dfrac{1}{2x}$~and~$Q = \dfrac{x}{x^{3 / 4} + 1}$

Now, we have integrating factor~$I . F . = e^{∫ Pdx}$

$= e^{- ∫ \dfrac{dx}{2x}} = e^{- \dfrac{1}{2}\log_{\mathrm{e}}x}$

$= e^{\log_{\mathrm{e}}x^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}} = x^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}$

Now, the solution of the linear differential equation is~$y $\times \left($I . F .\right) = ∫ Q $\times \left($I . F .\right)dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ x \cdotx^{- 1 / $2}\left($x^{3 / 4} + 1\right)dx + C$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ x^{1 / $2}\left($x^{3 / 4} + 1\right)dx + C$

Put~$x = t^{4} ⇒ dx = 4t^{3}dt$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = ∫ t^{2} \cdot4t^{3}dt \left($t^{3} + 1\right)$

$⇒ y $\cdot$x^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ $t^{2}\left($t^{3} + 1 - 1\$right)\left($t^{3} + 1\right)dt$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ t^{2}dt - 4 ∫ $\dfrac{t2}{t^{3} + 1}$dt + C$

Let,~$t^{3} + 1 = u ⇒ 3t^{2}dt = du$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = 4 ∫ t^{2}dt - $\dfrac{4}{3}$∫ $\dfrac{du}{u} +$C$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = $\dfrac{4t^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left|$u\right| + C$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = $\dfrac{4t^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left($t^{3} + 1\right) + C$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = $\dfrac{4x^{3 / 4}}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}} \left($x^{3 / 4} + 1\right) + C$

Now, the curve passes through~ \left(1, 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2\right)$

$⇒ 1 - \dfrac{4}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2 = \dfrac{4}{3} - \dfrac{4}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}2 + C$

$⇒ C = - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y \cdotx^{- 1 / 2} = \dfrac{4}{3}x^{3 / 4} - \dfrac{4}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(x^{3 / 4} + 1\right) - \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{4}{3}x^{5 / 4} - \dfrac{4}{3}\sqrt{x}\log_{\mathrm{e}}\left(x^{3 / 4} + 1\right) - \dfrac{x}{3}$

Hence, at~$x = 16,$~we get~

$y ( 16 ) = \dfrac{4}{3} \times32 - \dfrac{4}{3} \times4 \times \log_{\mathrm{e}}9 - \dfrac{4}{3}$

$⇒ y\left(16\right) = \dfrac{124}{3} - \dfrac{32}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}3$

$⇒ y\left(16\right) = 4\$left(\dfrac{31}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3}\log_{\mathrm{e}}$3\right) .$

$

questions.q: If a curve passes through the point  \left(1, - 2\right)$ and has slope of the tangent at any point~  \left(x, y\right)$ on it as $\dfrac{x^{2} - 2y}{x}$, then the curve also passes through the point
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^{2} - 2y}{x}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{2}{x}y = x$.~ It is in linear form.

I.F.$= e^{∫ \dfrac{2}{x}dx} = e^{2lnx} = x^{2}$

$∴ y . x^{2} = ∫ x . x^{2}dx = \dfrac{x4}{4} + c$

$∵$At $x = 1, y = - 2$,

$∴ - 2 \times {1}^{2} = \dfrac{\left(1\right)4}{4} + c$

$⇒ c = - 2 - \dfrac{1}{4} = - \dfrac{9}{4}$

$∴$curve is $y . x^{2} = \dfrac{x4}{4} - \dfrac{9}{4}$

$∴$It passes through \left(\sqrt{3}, 0\right)$.

$

questions.q:
$If $x=f(y)$ is the solution of the differential equation
\left(1+y^2\right)+\left(x-2 \mathrme^{\tan ^{-1} y}\right) \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}=0, y \in  \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$with $f(0)=1$, then $f \$left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dy}}+\frac{\mathrm{x}}{1+\mathrm{y}^2}=\frac{2 \mathrme^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}}}{1+\mathrm{y}^2} \\ & \text { I.F. }=\mathrme^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}} \\ & \mathrm{xe}^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}}=\int \frac{2\left(\mathrme^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}}\right)^2 \mathrm{dy}}{1+\mathrm{y}^2} \\ & \text { Put } \tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{t}, \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{1+\mathrm{y}^2}=\mathrm{dt} \\ & \mathrm{xe}^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}}=\int 2 \mathrme^{2 \mathrm{t}} \mathrm{dt} \\ & \mathrm{xe}^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}}=\mathrme^{2 \tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}}+\mathrm{c} \\ & \mathrm{x}=\mathrme^{\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}}+\mathrm{ce}^{-\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{y}} \\ & \because \mathrm{y}=0, \mathrm{x}=1 \\ & 1=1+\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=0 \\ & \mathrm{y}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}, \mathrm{x}=\mathrme^{\pi / 6}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $f$~be a differentiable function such that~$x^{2}f\left(x\right) - x = 4{∫}_{0}^{x}tf  \left(t\right)dt, f \left($1\right) = $\dfrac{2}{3}.Then~18f\left($3\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$x^{2}f\left(x\right) - x = 4{∫}_{0}^{x}tf\left(t\right)dt$

Now Differentiating both side~w.r.t.~$x$~we get,

$x^{2}f^{'} \left(x\right) + 2xf \left($x\right) - 1 = $4xf\left($x\right)$

$⇒ x^{2}f^{'} \left(x\right) - 1 = 2xf \left($x\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{2}{x}y = \dfrac{1}{x2}$~ \left(Lety = f \left($x\$right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$f^{'}\left($x\right)\right)$

Which is a linear differential equation,

So,~$I . F = e^{∫ - $\dfrac{2}{x}$dx} = e^{- 2lnx} = $\dfrac{1}{x2}

Now solution of the differential equation is given by,

\dfrac{y}{x2} =$∫ $\dfrac{1}{x4}$dx + C$

$⇒ $\dfrac{y}{x2} = - \dfrac{1}{3x^{3}} +$C$

Now given,~f\left($1\right) = $\dfrac{2}{3}

So,~\dfrac{2}{3} = - \dfrac{1}{3} +$C$

$⇒ C = 1$

Hence, the function will be,

f\left($x\right) = - $\dfrac{1}{3x} +$x^{2}$

So, the required value is given by,

18f\left($3\right) = $18\left[- \dfrac{1}{9} +$9\right] = 160$

$

questions.q: $Let $y = y  \left(x\right)$~be the solution of the differential equation $x\left(1 - x^{2}\$right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left($3x^{2}y - y - 4x^{3}\right) = 0, x > 1$~with y\left($2\right) = - 2$. Then y\left($3\right)$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $x\left(1 - x^{2}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3x^{2}y - y - 4x^{3}\right) = 0$

\left(x - x^{3}\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3x^{2} - 1\right)y = 4x^{3}$

\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \left(3x^{2} - 1\right)\left($x - x^{3}\right)y = 4x^{3} \left($x - x^{3}\right)$

This is a linear differential equation of the form~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} +Py = Q$

Here~$IF = e^{∫ Pdx} = e^{∫ \dfrac{3x^{2} - 1}{x - x^{3}}dx}$

Let~$x - x^{3} = t ⇒ IF = e^{∫ - \dfrac{dt}{t}}$

$= e^{- lnt} = \dfrac{1}{t}$

$∴ IF = \dfrac{1}{x - x^{3}}$

So the general solution of the differential equation will be~

$y \timesIF = ∫ Q \timesIFdx$

y\left(\dfrac{1}{x - x^{3}}\right) =$∫ $\dfrac{4x^{3}}{x - x^{3}} \ttimes$1\left($x - x^{3}\right)dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{4x^{3}}{\left(x - x^{3}\right)2}dx$

$= ∫ \dfrac{4x}{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)2}dx$

Now let~$I = ∫ \dfrac{4x}{\left(1 - x^{2}\right)2}dx$

Substituting~$1 - x^{2} = z$

$I = 2 ∫ \dfrac{- dz}{z2}$

$= - $2\left(- $\dfrac{1}{z}\right) +c = \dfrac{2}{1 - x^{2}} +c$

Hence the solution of the differential equation becomes~

$\dfrac{y}{x - x^{3}} = \dfrac{2}{1 - x^{2}} +c$

At~$x = 2, y = - 2$

$\dfrac{- 2}{2 - 8} = \dfrac{2}{1 - 4} +c$

$\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{- 2}{3} +c$

$∴ c = 1$

Hence the particular solution will be~$\dfrac{y}{x - x^{3}} = \dfrac{2}{1 - x^{2}} +1$

Put~$x = 3$

$\dfrac{y}{3 - 27} = \dfrac{2}{1 - 9} +1$

$\dfrac{y}{- 24} = - \dfrac{1}{4} +1$

$- \dfrac{y}{24} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$y = \dfrac{3}{4}\left(-24\right) = - 18$

$

questions.q: If& $y = \left(\dfrac{2}{π}x - 1\right)cosecx$~is the solution of the differential equation,~$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + p  \left(x\right)y = - $\dfrac{2}{π}$cosecx, 0 < x < $\dfrac{π}{2},then the function~$p\left(x\right)& is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Given $∫ \dfrac{f\left(x\right)}{log ⁡ \left(sin ⁡ x\right)}dx = log ⁡ [ log ⁡ sin ⁡ x ] + C$
By using anti differentiation method, we will get
$\dfrac{d}{dx} \left(log ⁡ \left[$log ⁡ sin ⁡ x\right] + c\right)$
$= $\dfrac{1}{log ⁡ \left(sin ⁡ x\right)}$⋅ $\dfrac{1}{sin ⁡ x}$⋅ cos ⁡ x$

questions.q: Let $y = y ( x )$ be the solution of the differential equation, ${\left(x^{2} + 1\right)}^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2x ( x^{2} + 1 ) y = 1$ such that $y\left(0\right) = 0 .$ If $\sqrt{a}y\left(1\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{32},$ then the value of $a$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
${\left(x^{2} + 1\right)}^{2}\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2x\left(x^{2} + 1\right)y = 1$
$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{2x}{x^{2} + 1}y = \dfrac{1}{{( x^{2} + 1 )}^{2}}$
Which is a linear differential equation with integrating factor
I.F. = $e^{∫ \dfrac{2x}{x^{2} + 1}dx} = e^{ln ( x^{2} + 1 )} = x^{2} + 1$
The solution of the given differential equation will be,
$y . \left(x^{2} + 1\right) = ∫ \left(x^{2} + 1\right) . \dfrac{1}{{\left(x^{2} + 1\right)}^{2}}dx = ∫ \dfrac{dx}{x^{2} + 1} = \tan^{- 1}x + c$
Now,~$y\left(0\right) = 0⇒ C = 0$ and $y = \dfrac{1}{( x^{2} + 1 )}\tan^{- 1}x$
$\sqrt{a}y ( 1 ) = \dfrac{\pi}{32} ⇒ \sqrt{a} = \dfrac{\pi / 32}{\pi / 8} = \dfrac{1}{4}$
$⇒ a = \dfrac{1}{16}$

questions.q: A function $y = f ( x )$ satisfies $f\left(x\right)sin2x + sinx - \left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)f^{'} \left($x\right) = 0$ with condition $f ( 0 ) = 0$. Then f\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right)is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$f\left(x\right)sin2x + sinx - \left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)f^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

Now, let $f\left(x\right) = y$ we get,

$⇒ ysin2x + sinx - \left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ ysin2x\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right) + sinx\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right) - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{1 + \cos^{2}x}\right)y = \dfrac{sinx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{∫ - \left(\dfrac{sin2x}{1 + \cos^{2}x}\right)dx}$

$⇒ I . F . = e^{log\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)}$

$⇒ I . F . = 1 + \cos^{2}x$

So, solution of the equation is given by,

$y\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right) = ∫ sinx\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right)dx$

$⇒ y\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right) = ∫ sinxdx$

$⇒ y\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right) = - cosx + C$

It is given that, $f\left(0\right) = 0$.

$⇒ 0\left(1 + 1\right) = - cos0 + C$

$⇒ C = 1$

$⇒ y\left(1 + \cos^{2}x\right) = 1 - cosx$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1 - cosx}{1 + \cos^{2}x}$

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1 - cos\dfrac{π}{2}}{1 + \cos^{2}\dfrac{π}{2}}$

$⇒ y\left(\dfrac{π}{2}\right) = 1$

questions.q: If for $x \ge 0, y = y  \left(x\right)$ is the solution of the differential equation, \left(x + 1\right)dy =  \left({ \left(x + 1\right)}^{2} +$y - 3\right)dx, y\left(2\right) = 0$ then $y\left(3\right)$ is equal to ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \left(1 + x\right) + \left(\dfrac{y - 3}{1 + x}\right)

\dfrac{dy}{dx} -1\left($1 + x\right)y = \left($1 + x\right) - $\dfrac{3}{( 1 + x )}

I.F$= e^{- ∫ $\dfrac{1}{( 1 + x )}$dx} = $\dfrac{1}{( 1 + x )}

$∴ $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{y}{1 + x}\right) =$x + $3\left($1 + x\right)- 1 + c$

$⇒ $\dfrac{y}{1 + x} =$x + 3 \left($1 + x\right)- 1 + c$

$⇒ y = \left($1 + x\right)\left[$x + $\dfrac{3}{( 1 + x )} +$c\right]$ , $∴$~at~$x = 2, y = 0$

$⇒ 0 = 3 \left(2 + 1 + c\right)$~$⇒ c = - 3$

At~$x = 3, y = 3$

questions.q: If the solution curve $y = y ( x )$ of the differential equation \left(1 + y^{2}\right)\left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)dx + xdy = 0, x > 0$ passes through the point $( 1, 1 )$ and $y\left(e\right) = \dfrac{\alpha - tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}{\beta + tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}$, then $\alpha + 2\beta$ is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: \left(1 + y^{2}\right)\left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)dx + xdy = 0$

$⇒ \left(1 + \log_{\mathrm{e}}x\right)xdx = - 1\left(1 + y^{2}\right)dy$

$⇒ ∫ \left(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{logx}{x}\right)dx + ∫ \dfrac{dy}{1 + y^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ logx + \dfrac{( logx{)}^{2}}{2} + \tan^{- 1}y = C$

This curve passes through the point \left(1, 1\right)$.

$⇒ log\left(1\right) + \dfrac{( log\left(1\right){)}^{2}}{2} + \tan^{- 1}\left(1\right) = C$

$⇒ C = \dfrac{π}{4}$

$⇒ logx + \dfrac{( logx{)}^{2}}{2} + \tan^{- 1}y = \dfrac{π}{4}$

Now, putting $x = e$

$⇒ loge + \dfrac{( loge{)}^{2}}{2} + \tan^{- 1}y = \dfrac{π}{4}$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}y = \dfrac{π}{4} - \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ y = tan \left(\dfrac{π}{4} - \dfrac{3}{2}\right)

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{tan\dfrac{π}{4} - tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}{1 + tan\dfrac{π}{4}tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}

$⇒ y = $\dfrac{1 - tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}{1 + tan\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)}

Hence, on comparing we get,

$⇒ $\alpha = \beta =$1$

$⇒ $\alpha +$2$\beta =$3$

$

questions.q: Let& $y = y\left(x\right), x > 1$,~be the solution of the~differential equation~\left(x - 1\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2xy = \dfrac{1}{x - 1}$, with~$y\left(2\right) = \dfrac{1 + e^{4}}{2e^{4}}$. If~$y\left(3\right) = \dfrac{e^{α} + 1}{\betae^{α}}$.~then the value of~$\alpha + \beta$ \text{ and } is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& \left(x - 1\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2xy = \dfrac{1}{x - 1}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{2x}{x - 1} \cdot y = \dfrac{1}{\left(x - 1\right)2}$

$I . F = e^{∫ \dfrac{2x}{x - 1}} = e^{2x} \times \left(x - 1\right)2$

Solution will be,

$y \times I . F = ∫ \dfrac{1}{\left(x - 1\right)2} \times I . F$

Solving above~with~$y\left(2\right) = \dfrac{1 + e^{4}}{2e^{4}}$~we get,

$y = \dfrac{1}{ \left(x - 1\right)2} \left[\dfrac{e^{2x} + 1}{2e^{2x}}\right]

So,~y\left($3\right) = $\dfrac{e^{6} + 1}{8e^{6}}, now on comparing with~y\left($3\right) = $\dfrac{e^{α} + 1}{\betae^{α}}~we get,~\alpha + \beta =$14$

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x - {y}^{2}}{y}, x\left(1\right) = 1,$ then $5x\left(2\right)$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x - {y}^{2}}{y}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x}{y} - y$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{1 + x}{y} = - y$

Now let $1 + x = t ⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{dt}{dy}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dy} - \dfrac{t}{y} = - y$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{∫ - \dfrac{1}{y}dy}$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{- logy}$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{log\dfrac{1}{y}}$

$⇒ IF = \dfrac{1}{y}$

So, the solution of the given differential equation is

$\dfrac{t}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{y} \times \left(- y\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{y} \times \left(- y\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = - y + c$

Also, $x\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{1} = - 1 + c$

$⇒ c = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = - y + 3$

Putting $y = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{2} = - 2 + 3$

$⇒ \left(1 + x\right) = 2$

$⇒ x = 1$

$⇒ 5x = 5$
questions.question: If $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x - {y}^{2}}{y}, x\left(1\right) = 1,$ then $5x\left(2\right)$ is equal to:
questions.explanation:
Given: $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x - {y}^{2}}{y}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{1 + x}{y} - y$

$⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{1 + x}{y} = - y$

Now let $1 + x = t ⇒ \dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{dt}{dy}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dt}{dy} - \dfrac{t}{y} = - y$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{∫ - \dfrac{1}{y}dy}$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{- logy}$

$⇒ IF = {e}^{log\dfrac{1}{y}}$

$⇒ IF = \dfrac{1}{y}$

So, the solution of the given differential equation is

$\dfrac{t}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{y} \times \left(- y\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = ∫ \dfrac{1}{y} \times \left(- y\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = - y + c$

Also, $x\left(1\right) = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{1} = - 1 + c$

$⇒ c = 3$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{y} = - y + 3$

Putting $y = 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left(1 + x\right)}{2} = - 2 + 3$

$⇒ \left(1 + x\right) = 2$

$⇒ x = 1$

$⇒ 5x = 5$
